faqs.question: What is the basic difference between a purohit and a jyotishi?
faqs.answer: Navdhya explains that a purohit is primarily a ritual specialist who conducts ceremonies, while a jyotishi focuses on horoscope reading, muhurta guidance, and astrological interpretation. Navdhya uses this kind of guidance to help families prepare more clearly, communicate better, and approach the ritual or booking process with greater confidence. That extra clarity also helps the household ask better follow-up questions and avoid avoidable confusion on the ceremony day.

faqs.question: Can one person be both a purohit and a jyotishi?
faqs.answer: Sometimes yes. Some practitioners are trained in both ritual performance and astrological consultation, but Navdhya still evaluates the primary strength needed for the family's actual requirement. Navdhya uses this kind of guidance to help families prepare more clearly, communicate better, and approach the ritual or booking process with greater confidence. faqs.question: When should a family book a purohit?
faqs.answer: A purohit is usually needed when the family is performing a puja, havan, samskara, house blessing, wedding rite, or ancestral ceremony that requires structured ritual guidance. Navdhya uses this kind of guidance to help families prepare more clearly, communicate better, and approach the ritual or booking process with greater confidence. That extra clarity also helps the household ask better follow-up questions and avoid avoidable confusion on the ceremony day.

faqs.question: When should a family consult a jyotishi?
faqs.answer: A jyotishi is useful when the family wants muhurta, horoscope insight, graha-related consultation, or timing guidance before a ceremony or major life decision. Navdhya uses this kind of guidance to help families prepare more clearly, communicate better, and approach the ritual or booking process with greater confidence. That extra clarity also helps the household ask better follow-up questions and avoid avoidable confusion on the ceremony day.
